title: Guardrail policy file
description: One policy file for a repository's guardrail gates. Gates are keyed by the ROLE they fill, not by the product that currently fills it, so replacing or renaming a product is a one-line edit rather than a schema break.

format.description: Default output format for `conductor run`. The --format flag overrides it.

product.description: Which product currently fills this role. gitleaks and osv-scanner are installed by the adopter, never by conductor.

enabled.description: Whether this gate runs. Defaults to true. A gate that is enabled but whose binary cannot be found is a blocking finding, never a silent skip.

enforce.description: Whether this gate's verdict reaches the exit code. Defaults to true. A gate with enforce false runs, reports, and appears in the text and SARIF output exactly as an enforced gate does, and never raises the exit code: neither its blocking findings nor its failure to run at all. This is the adoption ramp for a gate a repository is not ready to block on yet.

present-on-base.description: Only on the vulnerabilities gate. On a pull-request run osv-scanner also scans the base branch copies of the lockfiles that carry findings, and labels each finding introduced or present-on-base. block (the default when the key is absent) blocks on every finding; report reports present-on-base findings without blocking and blocks only on introduced ones. Read from the base branch policy on a pull request, so a pull request cannot set it for itself. Has no effect on a run without a base, where every finding blocks.

timeout-seconds.description: How long conductor lets this gate run before stopping it, in whole seconds, from 10 to 21600 (six hours, the GitHub-hosted job limit). Every spawn of the gate gets the full limit: the version probe, the scan, the intent gate's preparation steps and osv-scanner's base run. Absent means the default for the product: 120 for dep-guard, vault-guard and intent-guard, 600 for gitleaks, 300 for osv-scanner. A gate stopped at its limit could not run (timed-out). Read from the base branch policy on a pull request, so a pull request cannot change its own limit. The preview under the proposed rules also uses the base value, capped by its 300 second deadline. Not the same as a gate's own timeout flag under options.

stage.description: When this gate runs. Stages are cumulative in the order commit, push, ci: a gate runs at its own stage and at every later one, so a run at ci runs everything enabled. Defaults to commit for dependencies and secrets, and to ci for intent, secrets-history and vulnerabilities: the intent gate carries per-task ceremony, and a history scan or a registry lookup is pull-request work. A run with no --stage runs every enabled gate whatever its stage.

command.description: Absolute path to the gate's executable, overriding binary resolution. Use it to point at a build that is not on PATH.

args.description: Argument prefix placed before the arguments the umbrella adds. Only meaningful alongside `command`; without it the prefix is inferred from the resolved binary's name.

options.description: Handed to this gate unchanged. Each key is one of that gate's own long-flag spellings without the leading dashes; true renders as --key, false as --no-key, a scalar as --key value, and an array as one --key value pair per entry. The umbrella does not interpret any of them. Per-gate thresholds live here; there is deliberately no shared threshold, because the five products do not share one severity scale.
